title: Queuelift POC - Weekly retune and throughput review
next_steps: Priya to run 12-hour steady-state throughput run and upload perf logs
Jordan to share updated pilot pricing for burst capacity and dedicated lanes
Liam to provide sample production traffic replay and 95th/99th latency targets
action_items: Priya Shah: Run 12-hour steady-state throughput test with concurrency=18, adaptive batching on; upload perf logs to the pilot folder. Due: 2027-04-12
Jordan Ellis: Send updated burst capacity pricing (monthly vs hourly) and outline fallback policy options. Due: 2027-04-13
Liam Chen: Share 24h traffic replay and current latency SLO document (95th & 99th). Due: 2027-04-12
Amara Singh: Confirm VPC peering window for next week's ramp (security team availability). Due: 2027-04-14
header: Date: 2027-04-11 | Start: 10:30 PDT | Duration: 47m | Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (NimbleHealth), Amara Singh (NimbleHealth), Derrick Morales (NimbleHealth)
summary: Weekly POC check-in for the 'Queuelift' pilot focused on increasing steady-state throughput while keeping P95 latency within SLOs. Reviewed last week's run (spiky tails during 1-3pm replay), agreed to lower concurrency ceiling from 24->18 and enable adaptive continuous batching. Agreed next steps: 12-hour steady-state run, share perf logs, finalize burst pricing and schedule follow-up on 2027-04-18.
topics: Results from last weekend's mixed-load replay (spike behavior & P99 tail)
Tuning: concurrency targets, continuous batching profile, queue shaping
Operational asks: VPC peering timing, audit logs, and fallback policy
questions: Can Redwood keep P95 below 350ms at 6k RPS with adaptive batching on?
What's the expected token cost delta when moving from concurrency=24 to 18?
How quickly will the platform fall back to a smaller model in case of capacity pressure?
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Alright everyone, um, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, we got NimbleHealth and Redwood, yeah?
[00:12] Liam Chen: Yep, Liam here. Hey, uh, good morning.
[00:15] Amara Singh: Amara on my side.
[00:18] Derrick Morales: Derrick, product.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Priya from Redwood, SE. I'll run the perf bits after this.
[00:24] Jordan Ellis: Cool. So agenda — go over weekend replay results, talk concurrency + batching changes, and lock next run and owners. Sound OK?
[00:34] Liam Chen: Sounds good. Quick context — last run we saw sustained 4.8k RPS for about an hour but spikes to 7k caused the P99 to blow up, lots of KV cash misses and some queue pile ups.
[00:48] Priya Shah: Yeah, we dug into the traces — a lot of the P99s correlate with the cold KV cache, and then the queue depth hits the "soft limit" which forces larger batches that push latency up.
[01:10] Amara Singh: When you say "soft limit" can you define? Our infra folks want to know exact concurrency thresholds.
[01:18] Priya Shah: Sure. Right now the pilot config had a per-worker concurrency cap of 24, we saw queue depth hitting about 320 which made batch size jump to 64 per cycle. That amplified token compute.
[01:32] Derrick Morales: 64 sounds huge. So what's the plan? Drop concurrency?
[01:36] Jordan Ellis: The proposal is to lower the concurrency ceiling to 18, and enable adaptive continuous batching — so batches form quicker but with a tighter max size. The idea is to reduce tail amplification while keeping throughput.
[01:50] Liam Chen: Hmm, ok. Do we have an estimate on throughput loss? Last week you promised less than 10% reduction ideally.
[01:58] Priya Shah: From our microbenchmarks, moving 24->18 with adaptive batching usually cost 6-9% throughput but P95 improves drastically — like 200-300ms. There's a token-cost tradeoff because you do more, smaller batches.
[02:17] Amara Singh: Token cost is a big deal for procurement side. Can you quantify in dollar terms?
[02:22] Jordan Ellis: We'll quantify and send a short delta chart — monthlyized. Also, note burst capacity pricing vs dedicated lanes; that will be in the doc I send.
[02:33] Liam Chen: Another observation — some of the bad tails line up with large multi-turn conversations we replayed. KV cache warmup helped but not enough. Is there a way to prioritize prefix cache hits?
[02:48] Priya Shah: We have a priority pipeline for cache hits in our runtime — we can adjust the router to prefer requests with warm KV when under pressure. It's a config change (prefix-aware scheduling) not a code rewrite.
[03:04] Derrick Morales: Does that change fairness? We don't want some customers starving for predictable latency.
[03:10] Jordan Ellis: Right, so we add it as a weighted preference — the default policy remains fair but with slight preference for warm-KV requests when the queue cross threshold. We'll show backtest numbers.
[03:24] Liam Chen: Ok. Security question — we need audit logs, KMS integrated. You mentioned earlier the private stack supports HSM?
[03:32] Priya Shah: Yes, for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit logs. For the pilot on Redwood Dedicated, we can enable encrypted at rest keys and stream audit events to your SIEM.
[03:44] Amara Singh: Great, our security team still needs the SOC 2 snapshot and SAML SSO docs.
[03:50] Jordan Ellis: I'll attach SOC 2 and SAML guides after the call.
[03:54] Liam Chen: Thanks. Back to tuning — what's the expected behavior during a sudden surge where we exceed burst capacity? Will there be automatic fallback to a smaller model?
[04:03] Priya Shah: Yes, we have model-fallback policies. You can configure a cascade: primary model -> quantized variant -> smaller llama-family model. Fallback is latency-aware; we won't fallback preemptively unless latency objective is threatened.
[04:18] Derrick Morales: Is there any mellowing period for fallback? I don't want to flip models every minute.
[04:23] Priya Shah: We use hysteresis windows — default is 30s sustained breach before fallback, plus a backoff; can be tuned.
[04:34] Liam Chen: Ok, good. For the next run we said steady-state — what's the exact target?
[04:38] Jordan Ellis: Proposed: 12h steady-state at 5.5k RPS mean with 95th target <350ms. We'll cap concurrency at 18 and enable adaptive continuous batching with max batch size 40.
[04:52] Priya Shah: Also we'll enable prefix-aware scheduling and KV cache prewarm script from your replay.
[04:58] Amara Singh: Prewarm script — who runs that?
[05:00] Liam Chen: I'll run it; I'll provide the replay and the prewarm markers.
[05:03] Priya Shah: Perfect. Couple of notes — during earlier run the scheduler coalesced a lot of long running inferences which blocked the fast ones; we've isolated long-running paths in the runtime to reduce head-of-line blocking. But real-world replay helps validate.
[05:21] Jordan Ellis: We also noticed a couple of edge errors — some 503s during the spike window. Priya, do you have the stack traces?
[05:29] Priya Shah: Yeah, 503s stemmed from temporary resource starvation in one of the dedicated pods — we rebalanced the routing and added an additional worker in the middle of the run which helped. We'll mark that in the perf notes.
[05:40] Liam Chen: Can you capture metrics around queue depth and batch size over time? That would help our SRE to reason about autoscaling thresholds.
[05:47] Priya Shah: Absolutely — we'll include timeseries CSVs and a dashboard link.
[05:52] Derrick Morales: For fallbacks and model variants, are outputs still comparable? Product wants to ensure quality degradation is acceptable.
[05:59] Priya Shah: We'll run the same prompt set against the primary and fallback variant and include a small eval with similarity metrics and a human-rated sample. Should be in the perf pack.
[06:10] Amara Singh: Great. On the network side, when can we do VPC peering? Our security folks are only available next Thursday.
[06:17] Jordan Ellis: We can schedule peering then; it doesn't need to be before the steady-state run but would be preferred. We can run the test over the public peering with encrypted channels as a stopgap.
[06:29] Liam Chen: One more thing — can Redwood expose per-request token cost in logs so we can map cost back to feature area?
[06:36] Priya Shah: Yes, we have token-level attribution and can include that in the logs with correlated request IDs.
[06:43] Jordan Ellis: Alright, let's quickly recap owners and deadlines. Priya — you run the 12-hour steady-state test and upload logs by Monday. Jordan — pricing doc and SOC/SAML to the thread. Liam — traffic replay and SLOs by Monday. Amara — confirm peering availability.
[07:00] Liam Chen: Yep.
[07:02] Amara Singh: Yep.
[07:04] Derrick Morales: Quick question on pricing — your burst pricing, is that billed per second or per minute?
[07:10] Jordan Ellis: Burst is hourly by default but we can do per-minute granularity for short-term bursts — there is a premium though. I'll include both in the doc.
[07:20] Liam Chen: Ok. Any blockers on your side for the 18 concurrency change?
[07:24] Priya Shah: No blockers, it's a config flip, we can roll it out during the run.
[07:29] Derrick Morales: Cool. Also, uh, small transcription hiccup — we saw 'KV cash' in last notes; it's cache, not cash.
[07:37] (group laughter)
[07:40] Jordan Ellis: Noted. Anything else?
[07:43] Liam Chen: No, that's it from me.
[07:45] Amara Singh: Nothing else.
[07:47] Priya Shah: We'll add a couple of visualizations to the dashboard — queue depth, batch size distribution, per-worker concurrency.
[07:55] Jordan Ellis: Great. Scheduling — how about next Monday 10:30 again?
[07:58] Liam Chen: Works.
[08:00] Jordan Ellis: Awesome. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the perf pack.
[08:05] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains minor misrecognitions and speaker attribution may be approximate. Key artifacts referenced: shared pilot perf folder (link in CRM), SOC2 & SAML docs (Jordan to send), batch/tuning playbook (Redwood SE repo).
